transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Harris (Redwood AE), Owen Park (Redwood SE), Amir Patel (Verdant VP Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Verdant Platform Eng), Deepa Nair (Verdant Security Architect), Tom Blake (Verdant Network Lead)

Summary (auto): initial discovery focused on private deployment networking and compliance concerns, agreement to run a 4-week pilot; Redwood to send docs and compute/latency estimates.

Topics (auto): VPC peering, private endpoints, transit/hub design, region constraints for APAC, KMS integration, POC criteria.

[00:00] Maya Harris: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we should get started. quick roll call?
[00:08] Amir Patel: yeah, Amir here.
[00:09] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia on platform.
[00:10] Deepa Nair: Deepa, security.
[00:11] Tom Blake: Tom, networking.
[00:13] Owen Park: Owen from Redwood SE, hi.
[00:15] Maya Harris: cool, thanks. we sent a short agenda—network topology, security/KMS, region constraints, and POC ask. is that right Amir?
[00:24] Amir Patel: yeah that's right. main thing for us is we can't have user data leave APAC for legal reasons. so hosted cloud endpoints outside the region are a no-go.
[00:34] Maya Harris: understood. so Private deployment (private control plane + private data plane) is what we'll focus on — with VPC peering or private endpoints into your VPC depending on your preference.
[00:45] Tom Blake: quick question on peering — if we do peering to Redwood's VPC, do we need a cross-account route table? and how does egress look from our side?
[00:55] Owen Park: yeah great q. short answer: both peering and private endpoints are possible. peering will require route propagation and route table entries; if you want a hub-and-spoke we recommend Transit Gateway or cloud equivalent for scale. with private endpoints you get more control in a per-region setup and less route table sprawl.
[01:14] Sofia Ruiz: we use a hub transit in APAC already, so ideally Redwood sits in the same transit, or we peer into Redwood in each region. not sure on latency tradeoffs.
[01:25] Owen Park: latency wise, peering into a local Redwood node in the same region is lowest latency. if you route across transit gateways there's an extra hop but often still within, you know, single-digit ms depending on region. we'll run numbers for your expected QPS.
[01:41] Deepa Nair: on security, we need KMS integration and we need to ensure keys never leave our KMS. do you support customer-managed keys or HSM?
[01:52] Owen Park: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS integration. for hosted-like private deployments we support bringing your own keys via cloud KMS and in on-prem options we can integrate with HSMs. there's a config step in the deployment runbook.
[02:03] Amir Patel: perfect. also, audit logging — we need all inference requests logged for compliance, at least headers and request IDs. is that available?
[02:12] Owen Park: yes audit logs are available; we can stream them to your logging stack or push to S3 with encryption. there are options for token-level cost redaction if needed.
[02:23] Maya Harris: i'll drop the SOC2 + audit doc after this call.
[02:26] Speaker 2: uh right.
[02:29] Tom Blake: one more network detail—our CIDR range overlaps with one of the sample CIDRs you provided in the runbook. how do we handle NAT or ip translations?
[02:38] Owen Park: common issue. options: we can either adjust the sample CIDRs on our side, use NAT gateways, or use interconnect with NAT translation. if you have a large overlapping footprint, Transit Gateway with route translations usually simpler.
[02:51] Sofia Ruiz: got it. on bandwidth — our load is spiky. 1k rps peak for a short window, avg ~150 rps. we're very latency sensitive for sync user flows.
[03:03] Owen Park: that's helpful. we'll show batching and KV cache benefits — batching helps throughput but can increase tail latency. KV cache keeps session tokens locally which reduces re-compute.
[03:16] Amir Patel: KV cache — is that something we manage or Redwood?
[03:20] Owen Park: runtime handles KV cache in the serving tier, but you control TTLs and cache policies. we can expose metrics to your AppTeam.
[03:28] Deepa Nair: do you encrypt KV cache at rest? where are those caches stored?
[03:32] Owen Park: yes encrypted at rest; in private deployments we store caches within the customer's VPC or in an attached private volume depending on setup.
[03:41] [05:02] Maya Harris: sorry, small jump — i want to cover POC timeline. typical POC is 4 weeks: week 0 for network setup and access, week 1 for baseline latency runs, week 2 integrations and tooling, week 3 ramp + evaluation. does that align?
[05:17] Amir Patel: yes that seems reasonable. can Redwood provide a checklist for the week 0 network prep?
[05:22] Maya Harris: yes, i'll send a network checklist + terraform snippets for endpoints/peering.
[05:27] Tom Blake: is there a managed connector for our on-prem datacenter to the cloud? we have legacy infra for some services.
[05:35] Owen Park: we have options: direct connect / expressroute equivalents, or a VPN appliance. for low-latency on-prem traffic, dedicated interconnect tends to be best. we can surface a cost table.
[05:46] Sofia Ruiz: APAC regions — do you have nodes in Singapore and Tokyo? we need to make sure the region we pick is compliant with our data residency list.
[05:56] Owen Park: Redwood has regional nodes in ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) and ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo) for private deployments; we also support private control planes in customer VPCs if you need an air-gapped model.
[06:10] Amir Patel: good. we also have a regulatory requirement for regional failover — can't replicate data outside APAC. we need a plan for cross-region DR but within APAC only.
[06:21] Maya Harris: we can architect multi-az within the region and a secondary APAC region for DR. notes on replication policy will be in the runbook.
[06:30] Deepa Nair: what about egress inspection — we need to ensure outbound connections are restricted and that no unexpected telemetry goes to third parties.
[06:39] Owen Park: Redwood supports deny-list egress rules and we can lock down all external endpoints. for telemetry we can route logs to your S3 or syslog endpoint and we can turn off opt-in telemetry for PII.
[06:52] Tom Blake: latency numbers — can you give a ballpark for token perf vs model size?
[06:59] Owen Park: ballpark: for medium models in region, single token p50 is sub-20ms for short sequences, but it depends on batch size and kv cache hit rate; we'll run a model-specific table for you.
[07:12] Amir Patel: ok. cost side — we need an estimate comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private. our finance will want per-token and reservation pricing.
[07:20] Maya Harris: we'll include a comparative pricing sheet in the follow-up. for POC we can do short-term reserved capacity for predictability.
[07:28] Speaker 3: uh-huh.
[07:31] Sofia Ruiz: on IAM and RBAC — our SSO is SAML-based; can you integrate so our engineers only see the routes assigned to them?
[07:38] Owen Park: yes SAML and OIDC are supported. we support RBAC mapping and can tie to your groups for route and model-level permissions.
[07:46] Deepa Nair: do you have per-token redaction or tokenization logs retention policies? we need to limit retention to 30 days for this pilot.
[07:55] Owen Park: retention is configurable; we can set 30 days for POC and longer for production if needed.
[08:02] Maya Harris: okay quick demo ask — would you like a short topology sketch now or would you prefer a follow-up workshop?
[08:09] Amir Patel: follow-up workshop with our networking folks is better.
[08:13] Tom Blake: yes schedule deep-dive with networking — we'll have our transit diagrams.
[08:18] Maya Harris: great. we'll schedule a hands-on network workshop.
[08:21] Owen Park: also i want to note some edge cases — if you have overlapping IPv6 ranges we need to treat differently; those often show up in multi-cloud setups.
[08:32] Sofia Ruiz: we aren't live on ipv6 yet but good to know.
[08:36] Amir Patel: any blockers on our side we should know of?
[08:40] Owen Park: nothing yet; overlapping CIDRs and regulatory region constraints are the usual ones which you flagged.
[08:46] Maya Harris: ok lets capture next steps.
[08:48] [10:00] Owen Park: i'll run a quick throughput/latency estimate for your 1k peak vs avg and include the effect of batching and kv-cache, i'll also put recommended instance tiers for the expected workload.
[10:11] Maya Harris: i'll share the runbook + terraform samples + SOC2 artifacts.
[10:16] Amir Patel: we'll provide CIDRs and a transit diagram by tomorrow.
[10:21] Deepa Nair: i'll validate retention and provide a short compliance checklist.
[10:25] Sofia Ruiz: nice. anything on SSL/TLS certs handling? we terminate on our edge but want end-to-end TLS.
[10:32] Owen Park: end-to-end TLS supported; we can do mutual TLS between your VPC and Redwood endpoints if you require mTLS.
[10:40] Tom Blake: what about the model rollouts — can we pin models per route so QA uses a stable model?
[10:47] Owen Park: yes, model pinning and rollout policies (canary, A/B) are supported via the console or API. canary rollouts also have automatic fallback to a stable variant.
[10:59] Amir Patel: perfect.
[11:02] Maya Harris: i see a question in chat about on-prem packaging — we do have an on-prem package but requires more security review and longer lead time.
[11:11] Deepa Nair: we'd consider on-prem if the audit requirements tighten.
[11:14] Maya Harris: understood.
[11:16] [20:00] Speaker 4: can you, uh, share example network policies?
[11:23] Maya Harris: yes, included in the runbook i'll send.
[11:25] Tom Blake: also do you do health-checks/monitoring hooks? we'll want SLAs on latency and error rates.
[11:32] Owen Park: console provides per-route latency histograms, token-level cost, and tracing hooks to your APM. SLAs are available on Dedicated/Private contracts.
[11:43] Amir Patel: timeline for procurement — if POC looks good, we'd likely move to dedicated within 2–3 months. finance will want a roadmap and cost delta.
[11:53] Maya Harris: noted. we'll include a migration playbook from POC to dedicated.
[11:58] Sofia Ruiz: Anything else on region constraints? we need to ensure the control plane doesn't call out to external analytics endpoints.
[12:06] Owen Park: for private control plane we can host it in your VPC or in a private control plane within APAC only, so telemetry stays in-region.
[12:15] Deepa Nair: and that gives us better audit trail.
[12:18] Maya Harris: yes.
[12:20] [30:00] Owen Park: quick note — for the POC we'll propose two small models: a <light> model for low-latency user flows, and a larger model for batch/async processing, we'll include perf expectations for both.
[12:37] Amir Patel: ok that split maps to our use cases.
[12:40] Tom Blake: last network q — are there any special firewall rules for private endpoints?
[12:46] Owen Park: private endpoints use a set of managed ENIs; you'll need to allow the specific ENI IPs or prefix list; we can provide a managed prefix list to simplify updates.
[12:58] Sofia Ruiz: great.
[13:00] Maya Harris: ok i'm going to summarize and close — next steps are documented in action items; we'll send architecture doc, pricing and runbook by EOD tomorrow, schedule a hands-on networking workshop next week, and run latency/cost estimates.
[13:18] Amir Patel: thanks all, appreciate it.
[13:20] Deepa Nair: thanks.
[13:22] Tom Blake: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcript with some speaker mislabels and occasional word errors (e.g., "K-V cap" instead of KV cache). References: architecture doc link (sent in follow-up); runbook (to be shared).

Attachments referenced: https://redwood.example.com/rdw-private-deploy-runbook (placeholder), pricing-sheet-vl.xlsx (placeholder).
